aboutGame.title: What is War Footing?
paragraphs: War Footing is a turn-based strategy game from developer and publisher Strategist's Den Games in which you serve as a nation's Minister of Defense during an alternate-history Cold War crisis. Each turn represents one week, and you control the budget, the procurement contracts, the political relationships, and the force structure. The army that meets the invasion is the army you built before the first shot was fired.

Across eight scenarios you source equipment from foreign suppliers or your own domestic industry, raise units from company to brigade level from a catalog of more than 180 equipment types, and protect the political stability that keeps your funding line open. Battles resolve at the operational level, sector by sector and week by week, so readiness, doctrine fit, equipment quality, and deployment decide the outcome long before contact.

explore.title: Explore the War Footing Wiki
explore.description: Eight guide modules cover the whole mobilization: the beginner path, weekly economy management, equipment procurement, nations and blocs, combat doctrine, scenarios, diplomacy, and post-launch updates.

modules.name: War Footing Beginner Guide
modules.description: Learn the core gameplay loop, turn-based military planning, and how to prepare your nation for an invasion. Cover essential first steps, including budget management, equipment procurement, unit training, and force deployment.

highlights.detail: Read the briefing first: every scenario ships with different starting conditions, resource constraints, and an enemy configuration.
Audit the money before you spend it: available funds, recurring income, and every payment you already owe.
Lock in foundational procurement early, while availability is still favorable and prices have not moved.
Raise and train core formations so you field a combined-arms backbone instead of one expensive unit stack.
Stabilize domestic politics, because political stability is what keeps the funding line open.
Spend the final turns filling gaps and finalizing deployment before the invasion begins.

modules.name: War Footing Economy Guide
modules.description: Explain how to manage national income, allocate funds between procurement, industrial investment, domestic stability, and diplomacy, and plan purchases over multiple turns. Help players balance immediate military needs with long-term economic development.

highlights.label: Income
highlights.detail: Recurring income pays the every-turn readiness, training, and stability bills, so it has to stay above your obligations.

highlights.label: Capital
highlights.detail: Capital funding belongs to high-impact purchases and industrial expansion, never to routine operations.

highlights.label: Reserve
highlights.detail: The emergency reserve absorbs delayed income and sudden crises, so grow it before tensions rise, not during.

highlights.label: Stability
highlights.detail: Stability spending is a defensive investment: cut it and the funding stream that pays for your army can strangle itself.

modules.name: War Footing Equipment Guide
modules.description: Explore the game's military equipment categories, including infantry weapons, tanks, artillery, aircraft, and air defense systems. Compare equipment costs, combat capabilities, availability, and strategic trade-offs to help players make informed procurement decisions.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Infantry and armor first: infantry holds ground and forms the structure of every larger formation, while armor supplies breakthrough and holding power.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Air defense next: limited systems belong around your most important formations and infrastructure instead of being spread thin.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Artillery follows: indirect fire shapes engagements, but it cannot defend itself once it is overrun.

highlights.label: C
highlights.detail: Aircraft last: reach and striking power fade quickly without maintenance, crews, and sustained readiness.

modules.name: War Footing Nations Guide
modules.description: Introduce the playable nations and explain how their available units, industrial capabilities, and starting conditions affect military planning. Provide nation-specific preparation advice based on official game information and developer updates.

highlights.label: Blocs
highlights.detail: Cold War alignments decide who will sell to you and how quickly a foreign order can actually be delivered.

highlights.label: Industry
highlights.detail: Domestic production lines ramp up slowly but improve cost and self-sufficiency as they scale.

highlights.label: Standing
highlights.detail: Your starting treasury, industrial base, and neighbor determine which defense plan is even possible.

highlights.label: Doctrine
highlights.detail: Match the force you build to the doctrine and the threat your nation actually faces.

modules.name: War Footing Combat Strategy Guide
modules.description: Explain operational combat, sector defense, unit readiness, doctrine compatibility, and deployment decisions. Show how to build balanced forces and coordinate different unit types to improve battlefield effectiveness.

highlights.detail: Assign training weeks to the formations you will actually deploy, because readiness accumulates over turns.
Match doctrine to mission and re-role or re-equip a formation rather than hoping it adapts in the field.
Modernize key formations first so equipment quality can beat what is genuinely coming at you.
Deploy defensively near likely approaches and keep mobile forces back as reinforcement.
Cover every sector with a formation that is trained and fully equipped, not paper strength.
Recheck stability and the budget after the deployment order, because a war economy has to survive the war.

modules.name: War Footing Scenario Guide
modules.description: Introduce the game's eight scenarios and explain how different starting conditions, resource limitations, and enemy configurations influence the player's strategy. Provide preparation checklists and scenario-specific recommendations as verified details become available.

highlights.label: Briefing
highlights.detail: Eight scenarios ship with distinct starting conditions, resource constraints, and enemy configurations.

highlights.label: Opening
highlights.detail: The first turns set the rhythm: audit income, then commit to foundational procurement.

highlights.label: Midgame
highlights.detail: Raise and train the combined-arms backbone while political stability still holds.

highlights.label: Endgame
highlights.detail: Final turns are for filling gaps and finalizing deployment, since changes after the invasion barely matter.

modules.name: War Footing Diplomacy Guide
modules.description: Explain how diplomatic relationships, foreign suppliers, envoys, and political stability influence national defense planning. Help players understand the trade-offs between international procurement, diplomatic investment, and maintaining domestic support.

highlights.label: Envoys
highlights.detail: Diplomacy is worth the spend when extra preparation time is worth more than another purchase.

highlights.label: Treaties
highlights.detail: Honor diplomatic obligations early, while the political price of doing so is lowest.

highlights.label: Unrest
highlights.detail: Domestic unrest fractures a war economy faster than any enemy offensive can.

highlights.label: Deals
highlights.detail: Foreign deals buy speed and availability, while domestic industry buys control over your own supply.

modules.name: War Footing Updates and Roadmap
modules.description: Track official development announcements, balance changes, demo improvements, and planned post-launch content. Summarize confirmed updates and upcoming features using developer-published information rather than unverified community speculation.

highlights.label: Demo

highlights.label: Launch

highlights.label: Roadmap
highlights.detail: The developer posts update notes and roadmap announcements through the Steam store page and community hub.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about War Footing.

items.question: What is War Footing?
items.answer: War Footing is a turn-based strategy game from developer and publisher Strategist's Den Games in which you play a nation's Minister of Defense during an alternate-history Cold War crisis. You control the budget, the procurement contracts, the political relationships, and the force structure rather than individual units on a battlefield.

items.question: How long is one turn in War Footing?
items.answer: Each turn in War Footing represents one week, and every turn runs through the same six phases: review, budget, procure, train, deploy, and stabilize.

items.question: Do I fight the battles myself in War Footing?
items.answer: No. Combat in War Footing resolves at the operational level, sector by sector and week by week. Outcomes follow from unit readiness, doctrine fit, equipment quality, and where you chose to deploy before the invasion started.

items.question: How many scenarios and equipment types does War Footing have?
items.answer: War Footing ships with eight scenarios, each with its own starting conditions, resource constraints, and enemy configuration, plus more than 180 equipment types across small arms, armor, artillery, aircraft, and air defense systems.

items.question: What should I buy first in War Footing?
items.answer: Plan your first formations before you shop. Fund recurring readiness, training, and stability costs out of recurring income, reserve capital funding for major purchases, and never let installment payment dates collide with each other.

items.question: Where can I play War Footing and what does it cost?
items.answer: War Footing is a single-player, turn-based strategy game for Windows PC available on Steam. It released on October 15, 2026 at $11.99, a free demo is available, and the 10% introductory discount ran through October 22.
